mishnayos.summary: On Shavuos the two loaves come with two lambs. mishnayos.stIntro: On Shavuot there is an obligation to sacrifice burnt offerings, a sin offering, and peace offerings together with the offering of the two loaves. The burnt offerings consists of a bull, two rams, and seven sheep. A goat is brought for the sin offering. Two sheep are brought as peace offerings and waved together with the two loaves.

mishnayos.summary: The tamid and musaf offerings do not hold each other back. If the morning tamid or ketores was not brought, the afternoon one is still brought. Rabbi Shimon adds that a new mizbeach, Shulchan or Menorah is first used in a special way.

mishnayos.summary: The Kohen Gadol brings a mincha every day, half in the morning and half in the afternoon. If he died after the morning half, the new Kohen Gadol brings a whole new issaron and burns half. If no new Kohen Gadol was chosen yet, Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Yehuda argue who pays for it.

mishnayos.summary: Some menachos need both oil and frankincense, some only oil, some only frankincense, and some neither. The mishnah lists which are which.

chunks.en: Some need oil and frankincense,
chunks.st: There are four types of meal offerings: Those that require both oil and frankincense,

chunks.en: some need oil but not frankincense,
chunks.st: those that require oil but not frankincense,

chunks.en: some need frankincense but not oil,
chunks.st: those that require frankincense but not oil,

chunks.en: and some need neither oil nor frankincense.
chunks.st: and those that require neither frankincense nor oil. The mishna elaborates:

chunks.en: These need oil and frankincense:
chunks.st: And these are the meal offerings that require both oil and frankincense:

chunks.en: the mincha of fine flour,
chunks.st: The fine-flour meal offering, as it is stated:
chunks.stMore: “And he shall pour oil upon it, and put frankincense thereon” (Leviticus 2:1);

chunks.en: and the one made in a flat pan, and the one made in a deep pan,
chunks.st: the meal offering prepared in a pan (see Leviticus 2:5–6); the meal offering prepared in a deep pan (see Leviticus 2:7–10);

chunks.en: and the loaves and the wafers baked in an oven,
chunks.st: and the meal offering baked in an oven, which can be brought in the form of loaves or in the form of wafers (see Leviticus 2:4).

words.note: Thin crackers.

chunks.en: the mincha of Kohanim,
chunks.st: Additional meal offerings that require both oil and frankincense are the meal offering of priests;

chunks.en: and the mincha of the Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: the meal offering of the anointed priest,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the griddle-cake offering brought by the High Priest every day, half in the morning and half in the evening;

words.note: The Kohen Gadol.

chunks.en: and the mincha of non-Jews,
chunks.st: the meal offering of a gentile;

chunks.en: and the mincha of women,
chunks.st: a meal offering brought by women;

chunks.en: and the mincha of the omer.
chunks.st: and the omer meal offering (see Leviticus 23:15).

words.note: The barley offering brought on the second day of Pesach.

chunks.en: The mincha of nesachim needs oil,
chunks.st: The meal offering brought with libations that accompany burnt offerings and peace offerings requires oil

chunks.en: but does not need frankincense.
chunks.st: but does not require frankincense.

chunks.en: The lechem hapanim needs frankincense,
chunks.st: The shewbread requires frankincense

chunks.en: but does not need oil.
chunks.st: but does not require oil.

chunks.en: The two loaves,
chunks.st: The two loaves brought on the festival of Shavuot (see Leviticus 23:17),

chunks.en: the mincha of a sinner and the mincha of jealousy,
chunks.st: the meal offering of a sinner, and the meal offering of jealousy brought by a sota

chunks.en: need neither oil nor frankincense.
chunks.st: require neither oil nor frankincense.
chunks.stMore: The two loaves do not require oil or frankincense because these additions are not mentioned with regard to it. The meal offering of a sinner does not require them, as it is written: “He shall not put oil upon it, neither shall he give any frankincense upon it; for it is a sin offering” (Leviticus 5:11). With regard to the meal offering brought by a sota, it is similarly written: “He shall pour no oil upon it, nor give frankincense upon it, for it is a meal offering of jealousy, a meal offering of memorial, bringing iniquity to remembrance” (Numbers 5:15).

mishnayos.summary: Putting oil on a mincha of a sinner or of a sotah is an aveirah, and so is putting frankincense on it. Oil makes it pasul, but frankincense can be picked off. Putting oil on the leftovers, or a vessel of oil on top of its vessel, is not a problem.

chunks.en: He is punished for the oil by itself,
chunks.st: And if one places oil or frankincense on the meal offering of a sinner or on the meal offering of jealousy brought by a sota, he is liable to be flogged for violating the prohibition against placing the oil by itself,

chunks.en: and for the frankincense by itself.
chunks.st: and he is liable to be flogged for violating the prohibition against placing the frankincense by itself, as these are two separate prohibitions.

chunks.en: If he put oil on it,
chunks.st: If one placed oil upon the meal offering

chunks.en: he made it pasul. If he put frankincense,
chunks.st: he has disqualified it, but if one placed frankincense upon the meal offering

chunks.en: he should pick it off. If he put oil on its leftovers,
chunks.st: he should gather the frankincense and remove it. In this manner, the meal offering can be salvaged. Furthermore, one violates the prohibition only by placing oil on the meal offering prior to the removal of the handful; if he placed oil on its remainder

chunks.en: he does not break a "do not" mitzvah.
chunks.st: he does not violate a prohibition.

chunks.en: If he put a vessel on top of the vessel,
chunks.st: If one placed a vessel with oil on top of a vessel that contains a meal offering of a sinner or a meal offering brought by a sota

chunks.en: he did not make it pasul.
chunks.st: he did not disqualify the meal offering, as the oil was not placed on the meal offering itself.

mishnayos.summary: Some menachos need to be brought near the corner of the mizbeach (hagashah), some need waving (tenufah), some need both, and some need neither. Rabbi Shimon says that menachos with no handful taken also need no hagashah.

chunks.he: יֵשׁ טְעוּנוֹת הַגָּשָׁה וְאֵינָן טְעוּנוֹת תְּנוּפָה,
chunks.en: Some need to be brought near the mizbeach but do not need waving,
chunks.st: There are four categories of meal offerings: Those that require bringing near, a rite that requires the priests to carry the offering in their hands and bring it near the southwest corner of the altar, but do not require waving;

words.note: Bringing the mincha to the corner of the mizbeach.

chunks.en: some need waving but not bringing near, some need bringing near and waving,
chunks.st: those that require both bringing near and waving; those that require waving but not bringing near;

chunks.en: and some need neither waving nor bringing near.
chunks.st: and those that require neither waving nor bringing near. The mishna elaborates:

chunks.he: אֵלּוּ טְעוּנוֹת הַגָּשָׁה וְאֵינָן טְעוּנוֹת תְּנוּפָה,
chunks.en: These need bringing near but do not need waving:
chunks.st: And these are the meal offerings that require bringing near but do not require waving:

chunks.en: the mincha of fine flour,
chunks.st: The fine-flour meal offering;

chunks.en: and the one made in a flat pan, and the one made in a deep pan,
chunks.st: the meal offering prepared in a pan; the meal offering prepared in a deep pan;

chunks.en: and the loaves and the wafers,
chunks.st: the meal offering baked in an oven, which can be brought in the form of loaves or in the form of wafers;

chunks.en: the mincha of Kohanim,
chunks.st: the meal offering of priests;

chunks.en: the mincha of the Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: the meal offering of the anointed priest;

chunks.en: the mincha of non-Jews,
chunks.st: the meal offering of gentiles;

chunks.en: the mincha of women,
chunks.st: a meal offering brought by women;

chunks.en: and the mincha of a sinner.
chunks.st: and the meal offering of a sinner.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: The mincha of Kohanim
chunks.st: The meal offering of priests

chunks.en: and the mincha of the Kohen Gadol
chunks.st: and the meal offering of the anointed priest

chunks.en: do not need bringing near,
chunks.st: do not require bringing of the meal offering near to the altar,

chunks.en: because no handful is taken from them.
chunks.st: due to the fact that there is no removal of a handful in their sacrifice,

words.note: They are burned whole.

chunks.en: And whenever no handful is taken,
chunks.st: and there is a principle that with regard to any meal offering where there is no removal of a handful in their sacrifice,

chunks.en: there is no bringing near.
chunks.st: there is also no bringing near.

mishnayos.summary: Some things need waving but not bringing near, like the metzora's oil and asham, bikkurim, parts of shelamim, and the two loaves with the lambs of Shavuos. The mishnah explains how the waving is done. The omer and the sotah's mincha need both, and the lechem hapanim and the mincha of nesachim need neither.

chunks.he: אֵלּוּ טְעוּנִין תְּנוּפָה וְאֵין טְעוּנִין הַגָּשָׁה,
chunks.en: These need waving but do not need bringing near:
chunks.st: These are the items that require waving and do not require bringing near to the altar:

chunks.en: the log of oil of a metzora and his asham,
chunks.st: The log of oil that accompanies the guilt offering of a recovered leper and his guilt offering itself, as it is written:
chunks.stMore: “And the priest shall take one of the lambs and sacrifice it for a guilt offering, and the log of oil, and wave them for a wave offering before the Lord” (Leviticus 14:12);

words.note: A small measure, about the size of six eggs.
His guilt-offering korban.

chunks.he: וְהַבִּכּוּרִים כְּדִבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב,
chunks.en: and bikkurim, as Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says,
chunks.st: and the first fruits, in accordance with the statement of Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov;

words.note: The first fruits brought to the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.he: וְאֵמוּרֵי שַׁלְמֵי יָחִיד וְחָזֶה וָשׁוֹק שֶׁלָּהֶן,
chunks.en: and the parts for the mizbeach of a person's shelamim, with their chest and thigh,
chunks.st: and the sacrificial portions of the peace offerings of an individual and their breast and thigh, as it is written:
chunks.stMore: “The thigh of heaving and the breast of waving shall they bring with the offerings of the portions consumed by fire, to wave it for a wave offering before the Lord” (Leviticus 10:15).

words.en: and the parts for the mizbeach of

words.note: A peace offering that is shared by the mizbeach, the Kohanim and the owner.

chunks.en: whether of men
chunks.st: This requirement applies to peace offerings belonging both to men

chunks.en: or of women,
chunks.st: and to women,

chunks.en: for Jews but not for others,
chunks.st: by male Jews and not by others. The Gemara will explain this seemingly contradictory statement on 61b.

chunks.en: and the two loaves,
chunks.st: In addition, the two loaves and

chunks.en: and the two lambs of Shavuos.
chunks.st: the accompanying peace offering of two lambs brought on Shavuot also do not require bringing near but do require waving, as it is written:
chunks.stMore: “And the priest shall wave them with the bread of the first fruits for a wave offering before the Lord, with the two lambs” (Leviticus 23:20).

chunks.en: How does he do it?
chunks.st: How does one perform this waving?

chunks.he: נוֹתֵן שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם עַל גַּבֵּי שְׁנֵי כְבָשִׂים,
chunks.en: He puts the two loaves on top of the two lambs,
chunks.st: He places the two loaves on top of the two lambs

chunks.en: and puts his two hands under them,
chunks.st: and places his two hands below the loaves and the lambs,

chunks.en: moves them forward and back,
chunks.st: extends the offerings to each of the four directions and brings them back,

chunks.en: and raises them up and lowers them,
chunks.st: then raises and lowers them,

chunks.en: as it says (Shemos 29):
chunks.st: as it is stated with regard to the waving of the ram of the inauguration of the priests:

chunks.en: "which was waved and which was raised."
chunks.st: “Which is waved, and which is heaved up” (Exodus 29:27); i.e., waved back and forth, and heaved up and down.

chunks.en: The waving was done on the east side,
chunks.st: Waving was able to be performed to the east of the altar,

chunks.en: and the bringing near on the west side.
chunks.st: but the bringing near of meal offerings had to be done to the west, i.e., the southwest corner of the altar.

chunks.en: And the wavings come before the bringings near.
chunks.st: Also, with regard to all meal offerings, the wavings precede the actions of bringing near.

chunks.en: The mincha of the omer and the mincha of jealousy
chunks.st: The omer meal offering and the meal offering of jealousy brought by a sota

chunks.en: need waving and bringing near.
chunks.st: require both bringing near and waving. The meal offering of the omer requires waving, as it is written:
chunks.stMore: “And he shall wave the omer before the Lord” (Leviticus 23:11), and likewise with regard to the meal offering brought by a sota it is written: “And the priest shall take the meal offering of jealousy out of the woman’s hand and shall wave the meal offering before the Lord” (Numbers 5:25). The requirement of bringing near is derived as explained earlier.

chunks.en: The lechem hapanim and the mincha of nesachim
chunks.st: The shewbread and the meal offering brought with libations

chunks.en: need neither waving nor bringing near.
chunks.st: require neither bringing near nor waving.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Shimon says there are three korbanos that each have two of these three mitzvos: semichah (leaning hands), waving while alive, and waving after shechitah. He explains which two each one has.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: Three kinds need three mitzvos,
chunks.st: There are three types of offerings that require performance of three mitzvot.

chunks.en: two in each and every one,
chunks.st: Two mitzvot are performed on each and every one of them,

chunks.en: and the third one is not in them.
chunks.st: but the third mitzva is not performed in their
chunks.stMore: sacrifice, meaning that each of these offerings requires two out of the same three mitzvot, but not necessarily the same two as the others.

chunks.en: And these are they:
chunks.st: And these are the three offerings:

chunks.en: a person's shelamim,
chunks.st: Peace offerings brought as gift offerings by an individual,

chunks.en: and the shelamim of the community,
chunks.st: communal peace offerings, i.e., the two lambs brought with the two loaves on Shavuot,

words.note: The two lambs of Shavuos.

chunks.en: and the asham of a metzora.
chunks.st: and the guilt offering of a leper (see Leviticus 14:12–14).

chunks.en: A person's shelamim
chunks.st: Peace offerings brought by individuals

chunks.en: need semichah while alive,
chunks.st: require placing hands on the head of the animals while the animals are still alive,

words.note: Leaning both hands on the animal's head.

chunks.en: and waving after shechitah,
chunks.st: and waving when they are

chunks.en: but they do not have waving while alive.
chunks.st: slaughtered, but there is no obligation of waving them while they are alive.

chunks.en: The shelamim of the community
chunks.st: Communal peace offerings

chunks.en: need waving while alive and after shechitah,
chunks.st: require waving both while the animals are still alive and after they are slaughtered,

chunks.en: but they do not have semichah.
chunks.st: but there is no obligation of placing hands on them.

chunks.en: And the asham of a metzora
chunks.st: And the guilt offering of a leper

chunks.en: needs semichah and waving while alive,
chunks.st: requires placing hands and waving while the animal is still alive,

chunks.en: but it does not have waving after shechitah.
chunks.st: but there is no obligation of waving it after it is slaughtered.

mishnayos.summary: If someone promises to bring a mincha made in a machavas (flat pan), he may not bring one made in a marcheshes (deep pan), and the other way around. Two Rabbis explain the difference between the two pans.

chunks.en: If someone says, "I take upon myself a mincha made in a flat pan,"
chunks.st: One who takes a vow to bring a meal offering to the Temple and says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a meal offering prepared in a maḥavat,

words.note: A machavas.

chunks.en: he may not bring one made in a deep pan.
chunks.st: may not bring one prepared in a marḥeshet.

words.note: A marcheshes.

chunks.en: If he said "in a deep pan," he may not bring one made in a flat pan.
chunks.st: Similarly, if he says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a meal offering prepared in a marḥeshet, he may not bring one prepared in a maḥavat. The mishna clarifies:

chunks.en: And what is the difference between a flat pan and a deep pan?
chunks.st: What is the difference between a maḥavat and a marḥeshet?

chunks.en: Only that the deep pan has a cover,
chunks.st: A marḥeshet has a cover,

chunks.en: and the flat pan does not have a cover.
chunks.st: whereas a maḥavat does not have a cover;

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Yosei HaGlili says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

words.note: From the Galil.

chunks.en: Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: The deep pan is deep, and what is made in it is soft and moves about,
chunks.st: A marḥeshet is deep, and due to the large amount of oil, its product is soft because it moves about [roḥashin] in the oil.

words.en: and what is made in it

words.note: In a lot of oil.

chunks.en: and the flat pan is flat, and what is made in it is hard.
chunks.st: A maḥavat is flat, as the sides of the pan are level with the pan, and due to the small amount of oil, its product is hard.

words.en: and what is made in it

mishnayos.summary: If someone promises a mincha baked in an oven, he must bring one from a real oven, not from a small stove or tiles or pits; Rabbi Yehuda allows a small stove. If he promised a baked mincha, he may not bring half loaves and half wafers; Rabbi Shimon allows it.

chunks.en: If someone says, "I take upon myself a mincha baked in an oven,"
chunks.st: If one says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a meal offering baked in an oven,

chunks.en: he may not bring one baked on a small stove,
chunks.st: he may not bring a meal offering baked on a small oven [kupaḥ],

words.note: A kupach.

chunks.en: or baked on roof tiles, or baked in the pits of the Arabs.
chunks.st: nor a meal offering baked on roofing tiles, nor a meal offering baked in the baking pits of the Arabs.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: If he wants,
chunks.st: If he so wishes,

chunks.en: he may bring one baked on a small stove.
chunks.st: he may bring a meal offering baked on a kupaḥ.

chunks.en: If he said, "I take upon myself a baked mincha,"
chunks.st: If one says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a baked meal offering, without specifying loaves or wafers,

chunks.he: לֹא יָבִיא מֶחֱצָה חַלּוֹת וּמֶחֱצָה רְקִיקִין.
chunks.en: he may not bring half loaves and half wafers.
chunks.st: he may not bring half the required offering in the form of loaves and the other half in the form of wafers; rather, they must all be of one form or the other.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon allows it,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon deems this permitted,

chunks.en: because it is one korban.
chunks.st: due to the fact that both loaves and wafers are written with regard to this meal offering, which indicates that it is one offering of two possible forms.

mishnayos.summary: These menachos have a handful taken, and the leftovers are eaten by the Kohanim. Rabbi Shimon adds that when a Kohen brings a mincha of a sinner, a handful is taken, and both the handful and the rest are burned separately.

chunks.en: These are the menachos that have a handful taken, and their leftovers go to the Kohanim:
chunks.st: And these are the meal offerings from which a handful is removed and the remainder of the offering is eaten by the priests:

chunks.en: the mincha of fine flour,
chunks.st: The meal offering of fine flour;

chunks.en: and the one made in a flat pan, and the one made in a deep pan,
chunks.st: and the meal offering prepared in a pan; and the meal offering prepared in a deep pan;

chunks.en: and the loaves and the wafers,
chunks.st: and the meal offering baked in an oven that is brought entirely of loaves; and the meal offering baked in an oven that is brought entirely of wafers;

chunks.en: the mincha of non-Jews,
chunks.st: the meal offering of gentiles; and

chunks.en: the mincha of women,
chunks.st: the meal offering of women;

chunks.en: the mincha of the omer,
chunks.st: and the omer meal offering, i.e., the measure of barley brought as a communal offering on the sixteenth of Nisan;

chunks.en: the mincha of a sinner,
chunks.st: and the meal offering of a sinner; and

chunks.en: and the mincha of jealousy.
chunks.st: the meal offering of jealousy, brought by a sota.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.stMore: Although its remainder is not eaten by priests, as meal offerings of priests are burned in their entirety, as it is written: “And every meal offering of the priest shall be offered in its entirety; it shall not be eaten” (Leviticus 6:16), nevertheless,

chunks.en: The mincha of a sinner of Kohanim has a handful taken,
chunks.st: with regard to the meal offering of a sinner brought by one of the priests, a handful is removed.

chunks.en: and the handful is burned by itself,
chunks.st: And the handful is sacrificed on the altar by itself,

chunks.en: and the leftovers are burned by themselves.
chunks.st: and the remainder is sacrificed on the altar by itself.

mishnayos.summary: Some menachos go only on the mizbeach and nothing goes to the Kohanim; here the mizbeach has the bigger share. The two loaves and the lechem hapanim go only to the Kohanim; here the Kohanim have the bigger share.

chunks.he: מִנְחַת כֹּהֲנִים וּמִנְחַת כֹּהֵן מָשִׁיחַ וּמִנְחַת נְסָכִים,
chunks.en: The mincha of Kohanim, the mincha of the Kohen Gadol, and the mincha of nesachim
chunks.st: The meal offering of priests, the meal offering of the anointed priest, i.e., the High Priest, and the meal offering brought with libations that accompany burnt offerings and peace offerings

chunks.en: go to the mizbeach, and none of them goes to the Kohanim.
chunks.st: are burned in their entirety on the altar, and there is no part of them for the priests.

chunks.he: בָּזֶה יָפֶה כֹחַ הַמִּזְבֵּחַ מִכֹּחַ הַכֹּהֲנִים.
chunks.en: In this, the mizbeach has more power than the Kohanim.
chunks.st: And in the case of those offerings, the power of the altar is greater than the power of the priests.

chunks.en: The two loaves and the lechem hapanim
chunks.st: The two loaves, i.e., the public offering on Shavuot of two loaves baked from new wheat, and the shewbread,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the twelve loaves that were placed on the sacred Table in the Sanctuary each Shabbat,

chunks.en: go to the Kohanim, and none of them goes to the mizbeach.
chunks.st: are eaten by the priests, and there is no part of them burned on the altar.

chunks.he: וּבָזֶה יָפֶה כֹחַ הַכֹּהֲנִים מִכֹּחַ הַמִּזְבֵּחַ:
chunks.en: And in this, the Kohanim have more power than the mizbeach.
chunks.st: And in the case of those offerings, the power of the priests is greater than the power of the altar.

mishnayos.summary: Menachos made in a vessel get oil three times: poured on, mixed in, and put in the vessel first. Rebbi and the Sages argue whether the oil is mixed with the loaves or with the flour. Wafers are smeared with oil in the shape of an X.

chunks.en: All the menachos that are made in a vessel
chunks.st: All the meal offerings that are prepared in a vessel, e.g., the offerings prepared in a pan or deep pan,

chunks.en: need three placings of oil:
chunks.st: require three placements of oil, listed here in the reverse order of their placement:

chunks.en: pouring, and mixing,
chunks.st: Pouring oil on the cakes after they have been cooked, and mixing oil into the flour,

chunks.en: and putting oil in the vessel before they are made.
chunks.st: and placement of oil into the vessel prior to preparation of the meal offerings.

chunks.en: And he mixes the loaves with the oil;
chunks.explain: First he bakes the loaves and breaks them, then mixes in oil.
chunks.st: In the meal offerings that come as loaves, it is after the flour has been baked into loaves that one breaks them into pieces and mixes them with oil;

chunks.en: that is what Rebbi says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi.

words.note: Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi, who wrote down the Mishnah.

chunks.en: But the Sages say:
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: He mixes the fine flour. The loaves need mixing,
chunks.st: It is with fine flour that one mixes the oil. Although the loaves of the meal offering baked in an oven require mixing of their flour with oil,

chunks.en: but the wafers are smeared.
chunks.st: wafers do not require mixing, but rather a smearing of oil on them after baking.

chunks.en: How does he smear them?
chunks.st: How does one smear oil on them?

chunks.en: In the shape of an X.
chunks.st: He does so in a shape similar to the Greek letter chi, Χ,

words.note: A Greek letter shaped like an X.

chunks.en: And the rest of the oil is eaten by the Kohanim.
chunks.st: and the rest of the oil remaining after smearing is eaten by priests.

Rabbi Meir says all are twelve except the todah and the nazir's loaves, which are ten.

chunks.st: All the meal offerings require

chunks.st: rubbing three hundred times

chunks.en: and five hundred poundings.
chunks.st: and striking five hundred times with one’s fist or palm.

words.note: Hitting it with a fist.

chunks.en: The rubbing and the pounding are done to the wheat kernels.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says:
chunks.st: And Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.st: which come as ten each.

mishnayos.summary: The omer was one issaron of flour taken from three se'ah of barley. The two loaves were two issaron from three se'ah, and the lechem hapanim was twenty-four issaron from twenty-four se'ah.

chunks.he: הָעֹמֶר הָיָה בָא עִשָּׂרוֹן מִשָּׁלשׁ סְאִין.
chunks.en: The omer came as one issaron from three se'ah.
chunks.st: The omer offering, i.e., the measure of barley brought as a communal offering on the sixteenth of Nisan, would come from a tenth of an ephah of flour sifted from three se’a of barley.

words.note: A big measure of grain.

chunks.en: The two loaves,
chunks.st: The two loaves would come from

chunks.en: two issaron from three se'ah.
chunks.st: two-tenths of an ephah of flour sifted from three se’a of wheat.

chunks.en: The lechem hapanim,
chunks.st: The shewbread would come from

chunks.he: עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה עֶשְׂרוֹנִים מֵעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע סְאִין:
chunks.en: twenty-four issaron from twenty-four se'ah.
chunks.st: twenty-four tenths of an ephah of flour sifted from twenty-four se’a of wheat.

mishnayos.summary: The flour of the omer was sifted through thirteen sifters, the two loaves through twelve, and the lechem hapanim through eleven. Rabbi Shimon says there was no set number; they sifted until it was as fine as it needed to be.

chunks.he: הָעֹמֶר הָיָה מְנֻפֶּה בִּשְׁלשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה נָפָה.
chunks.en: The omer was sifted with thirteen sifters.
chunks.st: The flour of the omer was sifted with thirteen sifters,
chunks.stMore: each finer than its predecessor, and the flour that emerged from the final sifter was sacrificed.

words.note: Together: thirteen.

chunks.en: And the two loaves with twelve.
chunks.st: The flour of the two loaves was sifted with twelve sifters,

chunks.en: And the lechem hapanim with eleven.
chunks.st: and the flour of the shewbread was sifted with eleven sifters.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: It had no set number.
chunks.st: They have no fixed number of sifters;

chunks.he: אֶלָּא סֹלֶת מְנֻפָּה כָּל צָרְכָּהּ הָיָה מֵבִיא,
chunks.en: Rather, he would bring fine flour sifted as much as it needed,
chunks.st: rather, it was fine flour that was completely sifted that one would bring for all of these offerings,

chunks.en: as it says (Vayikra 24):
chunks.st: as it is stated: “

chunks.en: "And you shall take fine flour and bake it,"
chunks.st: And you shall take fine flour and bake it” (Leviticus 24:5),

chunks.en: meaning, until it is sifted as much as it needs.
chunks.st: indicating that one does not fulfill his obligation until the flour will be completely sifted.

mishnayos.summary: The todah comes with forty loaves: ten chametz loaves and thirty matzah loaves of three kinds (ten of each). The mishnah explains how much flour is used for each kind, in two kinds of measures.

chunks.he: הַתּוֹדָה הָיְתָה בָאָה חָמֵשׁ סְאִין יְרוּשַׁלְמִיּוֹת,
chunks.en: The todah came with five Yerushalayim se'ah,
chunks.st: The flour for the loaves accompanying the thanks offering would come from a measure of five Jerusalem se’a offering,

words.note: The se'ah used later in Yerushalayim was bigger.

chunks.en: which are six se'ah of the midbar,
chunks.st: which are equivalent to six wilderness se’a.
chunks.stMore: The se’a referred to in the Bible when the Jewish people were in the wilderness is smaller than the se’a used later in Jerusalem.

chunks.en: which are two eifos,
chunks.st: This is equivalent to two ephahs,

words.note: A big measure of flour.

chunks.en: each eifah being three se'ah,
chunks.st: each ephah being three wilderness se’a.

chunks.en: which make twenty issaron:
chunks.st: These two ephahs are twenty measures of a tenth of an ephah.

chunks.en: ten for the chametz and ten for the matzah.
chunks.st: Ten of these tenths were used to make leavened loaves and ten of these tenths were used to make unleavened loaves, i.e., matza. The mishna elaborates:

chunks.en: Ten for the chametz,
chunks.st: There are ten tenths for the loaves of leavened bread,

chunks.en: one issaron for each loaf.
chunks.st: a tenth of an ephah per loaf.

chunks.en: And ten for the matzah,
chunks.st: And there are ten tenths for the loaves of matza.

chunks.en: and in the matzah there are three kinds:
chunks.st: And among the loaves of matza there are three types:

chunks.en: loaves, wafers, and soaked loaves.
chunks.st: Loaves, wafers, and those poached in water, ten loaves of each type.

words.note: Made from flour mixed in hot water.

chunks.he: נִמְצְאוּ שְׁלשָׁה עֶשְׂרוֹנוֹת וּשְׁלִישׁ לְכָל מִין,
chunks.en: So it turns out three and a third issaron for each kind,
chunks.st: Consequently, there are three-and-one-third tenths of an ephah for each and every type,

chunks.en: three loaves for each issaron.
chunks.st: three loaves per tenth of an ephah.

chunks.en: In the Yerushalayim measure, there were thirty kav:
chunks.st: And in the Jerusalem measure there were thirty kav,

words.note: A smaller measure.

chunks.en: fifteen for the chametz,
chunks.st: fifteen kav for the loaves of leavened bread

words.note: Together: fifteen.

chunks.en: and fifteen for the matzah.
chunks.st: and fifteen for the loaves of matza. The mishna elaborates:

chunks.en: Fifteen for the chametz,
chunks.st: There are fifteen kav for the loaves of leavened bread,

chunks.en: a kav and a half for each loaf.
chunks.st: one and one-half kav per loaf.

chunks.en: And fifteen for the matzah,
chunks.st: And there are fifteen kav for the loaves of matza.

chunks.en: and the matzah has three kinds:
chunks.st: And among the loaves of matza there are three types:

chunks.en: loaves, wafers, and soaked loaves.
chunks.st: Loaves, wafers, and those poached in water.

chunks.en: So it turns out five kav for each kind,
chunks.st: Consequently, there are five kav for each and every type,

chunks.en: two loaves for each kav.
chunks.st: two loaves per kav.

mishnayos.summary: The loaves of the miluim (when the Kohanim started serving in the Mishkan) were like the todah's matzah. The nazir brings only two kinds of matzah. One loaf of each kind of the todah is given as terumah to the Kohen who sprinkled the blood, and the rest is eaten by the owners.

chunks.en: The miluim came like the matzah of the todah:
chunks.st: The loaves that accompanied the ram of the inauguration of the Tabernacle would come parallel to the three types of matza that accompany the thanks offering:

words.note: The korbanos brought when the Mishkan was first set up.

chunks.en: loaves, wafers, and soaked loaves.
chunks.st: Loaves, wafers, and loaves poached in water and made with oil (see Leviticus 8:26).
chunks.stMore: The loaves of leavened bread that accompany the thanks offering were not brought with the ram of inauguration.

chunks.en: The nazir's loaves came as
chunks.st: The loaves that accompany the offering that the nazirite brings upon completion of his period of naziriteship would come

chunks.en: two parts of the matzah of the todah:
chunks.st: with only two parts of the three types of matza that accompany the thanks offering, namely,

chunks.en: loaves and wafers,
chunks.st: loaves and wafers,

chunks.en: but it has no soaked loaves.
chunks.st: but there is no matza poached in water (see Numbers 6:15).

chunks.en: So it turns out ten Yerushalayim kav,
chunks.st: Consequently, the loaves of the offering of a nazirite are from ten kav of fine flour according to the Jerusalem
chunks.stMore: measure, as taught in the previous mishna that each type of the loaves of matza comes from five kav of flour,

chunks.en: which are six issaron and a bit more.
chunks.st: which equal six-and-two-thirds tenths
chunks.stMore: of an ephah according to the wilderness measure, as each type of the loaves of matza comes from three-and-one-third tenths of an ephah.

words.note: Two thirds more.

chunks.he: וּמִכֻּלָּן הָיָה נוֹטֵל אֶחָד מֵעֲשָׂרָה תְּרוּמָה,
chunks.en: And from all of them he took one out of ten as terumah,
chunks.st: From all of the four types of loaves accompanying the thanks offering, one takes one loaf from each set of ten as teruma, to be given to a priest,

chunks.en: as it says (Vayikra 7):
chunks.st: as it is stated: “

chunks.he: וְהִקְרִיב מִמֶּנּוּ אֶחָד מִכָּל קָרְבָּן תְּרוּמָה לַה'.
chunks.en: "And he shall bring from it one of each korban as terumah to Hashem."
chunks.st: And he shall present from it one of each offering as a teruma unto the Lord;
chunks.stMore: to the priest that sprinkles the blood of the peace offerings against the altar it shall be given” (Leviticus 7:14). The verse is analyzed:

chunks.en: "One" means he should not take a broken piece.
chunks.st: “One” indicates that one should not take a sliced loaf;

chunks.en: "Of each korban" means
chunks.st: “of each offering” indicates

chunks.en: that all the korbanos should be equal,
chunks.st: that all the offerings should be equal, i.e.,

chunks.en: and he should not take from one kind for another.
chunks.st: that one should not take a loaf from one type of offering for another type;

chunks.he: לַכֹּהֵן הַזֹּרֵק אֶת דַּם הַשְּׁלָמִים לוֹ יִהְיֶה,
chunks.en: "To the Kohen who sprinkles the blood of the shelamim it shall be,"
chunks.st: “to the priest that sprinkles the blood of the peace offerings against the altar it shall be given,”

chunks.en: and the rest is eaten by the owners.
chunks.st: and the rest of the loaves are eaten by the owner.

mishnayos.summary: The loaves of the todah become holy only when the todah is shechted properly while the loaves are inside the wall and already baked with a crust. The mishnah lists cases where the loaves do or do not become holy.

chunks.en: If one shechts the todah inside,
chunks.st: In the case of one who slaughters the thanks offering in its proper place inside the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: and its loaves are outside the wall,
chunks.st: and at that time its forty loaves were outside the wall,

chunks.en: the loaves do not become holy.
chunks.st: the loaves were not consecrated.

chunks.en: If he shechted it before they formed a crust in the oven,
chunks.st: Likewise, if he slaughtered the thanks offering before the surface of the loaves formed a crust in the oven,

chunks.he: וַאֲפִלּוּ קָרְמוּ כֻלָּן חוּץ מֵאַחַד מֵהֶן,
chunks.en: and even if all of them formed a crust except one of them,
chunks.st: and even if the surface of all the loaves formed a crust except for one of them,

chunks.en: the loaves do not become holy.
chunks.st: the loaves were not consecrated.

chunks.en: If he shechted it planning for outside its time or outside its place,
chunks.st: If one slaughtered the thanks offering with the intent to partake of it or to burn the sacrificial portions beyond its designated time or outside its designated area, and the offering was rendered piggul or was disqualified, respectively,

chunks.en: the loaves do become holy.
chunks.st: the loaves were consecrated and either rendered piggul or disqualified.

chunks.en: If he shechted it and it turned out to be a treifah,
chunks.st: If one slaughtered the thanks offering and it was discovered that it was an animal with a wound that would have caused it to die within twelve months [tereifa],

words.note: An animal with a deadly injury.

chunks.en: the loaves do not become holy.
chunks.st: the loaves were not consecrated, as the cause of the animal’s disqualification preceded its slaughter.

chunks.en: If he shechted it and it turned out to have a mum,
chunks.st: If one slaughtered the thanks offering and it was discovered that it is a blemished
chunks.stMore: animal that may not be sacrificed ab initio but if it ascended the altar it may be sacrificed,

words.note: A blemish that makes it not fit for a korban.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: They become holy. But the Sages say:
chunks.st: He has consecrated the loaves, since if the offering ascends the altar it is sacrificed. And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: They do not become holy.
chunks.st: He has not consecrated the loaves, since it may not be sacrificed ab initio.

chunks.en: If he shechted it not for its own sake,
chunks.st: If one slaughtered the thanks offering not for its sake but for the sake of another offering,

chunks.en: and so too the ram of the miluim,
chunks.st: and likewise, if one slaughtered the ram of inauguration not for its sake,

chunks.he: וְכֵן שְׁנֵי כִבְשֵׂי עֲצֶרֶת שֶׁשְּׁחָטָן שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָן,
chunks.en: and so too the two lambs of Shavuos that he shechted not for their own sake,
chunks.st: and likewise, if one slaughtered the communal peace offering of two sheep that accompany the two loaves on Shavuot not for their sake,

chunks.en: the loaves do not become holy.
chunks.st: the loaves were not consecrated.

mishnayos.summary: If nesachim became holy in a vessel and the korban turned out to be pasul, they can go with another korban; otherwise they become pasul overnight. A todah's baby, its temurah, or a replacement todah do not need loaves.

chunks.he: נְסָכִין שֶׁקָּדְשׁוּ בִכְלִי וְנִמְצָא הַזֶּבַח פָּסוּל,
chunks.en: Nesachim that became holy in a vessel, and the korban turned out to be pasul:
chunks.st: In a case where the libations that accompany the offerings were sanctified in a service vessel when the animal was slaughtered and the offering was discovered to be unfit,

chunks.en: if there is another korban there,
chunks.st: if there is another offering that was slaughtered and requires libations,

chunks.en: they should be brought with it.
chunks.st: the libations should be sacrificed with that offering;

chunks.en: And if not,
chunks.st: and if not,

chunks.en: they become pasul by staying overnight.
chunks.st: they should be disqualified by being left overnight, and then burned.

chunks.en: The baby of a todah, and its temurah,
chunks.st: With regard to the offspring of an animal designated as a thanks offering, or an animal that is its substitute;

words.note: An animal someone tried to swap for a korban; it also becomes holy.

chunks.he: וְהַמַּפְרִישׁ תּוֹדָתוֹ וְאָבְדָה וְהִפְרִישׁ אַחֶרֶת תַּחְתֶּיהָ,
chunks.en: and one who set aside his todah and it got lost, and he set aside another one in its place,
chunks.st: or in a case where one separated an animal as a thanks offering and it was lost and he separated another in its stead,
chunks.stMore: and the first animal was then found, in all three cases, the second animal, i.e., the offspring, the substitute, or the replacement, is sacrificed,

words.en: and the one who sets aside

chunks.en: do not need loaves,
chunks.st: but it does not require the bringing of accompanying loaves.

chunks.en: as it says (Vayikra 7):
chunks.st: This is as it is stated: “If he sacrifices it for a thanks offering,

chunks.en: "And he shall bring with the todah korban" loaves.
chunks.st: then he shall sacrifice with the thanks offering
chunks.stMore: unleavened cakes mingled with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil, and cakes mingled with oil, of fine flour poached” (Leviticus 7:12).

chunks.en: The todah needs loaves,
chunks.st: The verse indicates that the initial thanks offering requires loaves,

chunks.en: but not its baby and not its replacement,
chunks.st: but neither its offspring, nor its replacement,

chunks.en: and not its temurah need loaves.
chunks.st: nor its substitute requires loaves.

mishnayos.summary: If someone promises a todah, he must pay for it and its loaves from regular money, not from maaser sheni money. If he said he would bring it from maaser sheni, he may do so, but the loaves must be bought with maaser sheni money, not made from maaser sheni wheat.

chunks.en: If someone says, "I take upon myself a todah,"
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a thanks offering,

chunks.en: he must bring it and its loaves from chullin.
chunks.st: must bring it and its loaves from non-sacred money in his possession and not second-tithe money.
chunks.stMore: Since he said: It is incumbent upon me, bringing the offering is an obligation, and one may not fulfill an obligation with second-tithe money.

words.note: Regular money, not maaser sheni.

chunks.he: תּוֹדָה מִן הַחֻלִּין וְלַחְמָהּ מִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר,
chunks.en: If he said "a todah from chullin and its loaves from maaser,"
chunks.st: If one said: It is incumbent upon me to bring a thanks offering from non-sacred money and its loaves from second-tithe money,

words.note: Maaser sheni money, which must be used in Yerushalayim.

chunks.en: he must bring it and its loaves from chullin.
chunks.st: he must bring the thanks offering and its loaves from non-sacred money.

chunks.he: תּוֹדָה מִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר וְלַחְמָהּ מִן הַחֻלִּין,
chunks.en: If he said "a todah from maaser and its loaves from chullin,"
chunks.st: If one said: It is incumbent upon me to bring a thanks offering from second-tithe money and its loaves from non-sacred money,

chunks.he: יָבִיא. הַתּוֹדָה הִיא וְלַחְמָהּ מִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר,
chunks.en: he may bring it that way. If he said "the todah, it and its loaves, from maaser,"
chunks.st: he may bring it in that manner. Likewise, if one said: It is incumbent upon me to bring a thanks offering and its loaves from second-tithe money,

chunks.he: יָבִיא. וְלֹא יָבִיא מֵחִטֵּי מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי,
chunks.en: he may bring it that way. But he may not bring them from maaser sheni wheat,
chunks.st: he may bring it in that manner. And he may not bring the loaves from second-tithe wheat;

chunks.en: only with maaser sheni money.
chunks.st: rather, he purchases the flour with second-tithe money.

mishnayos.summary: Something a person must bring because of a promise must be bought with regular money, not maaser sheni. We learn this from the korban Pesach, which is an obligation and is brought only from regular money. Nesachim always come from regular money.

chunks.en: From where do we know that one who says "I take upon myself a todah"
chunks.st: From where is it derived with regard to one who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a thanks offering,

chunks.en: may bring it only from chullin?
chunks.st: that he may bring it only from non-sacred money?

chunks.en: As it says (Devarim 16):
chunks.st: It is derived from a verse, as the verse states: “

chunks.he: וְזָבַחְתָּ פֶּסַח לַה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ צֹאן וּבָקָר,
chunks.en: "You shall bring a korban Pesach to Hashem your G-d, sheep and cattle."
chunks.st: And you shall sacrifice the Paschal offering to the Lord your God, of the flock and the herd” (Deuteronomy 16:2). The verse is difficult:

chunks.en: But doesn't the Pesach come
chunks.st: Doesn’t the Paschal offering come

chunks.en: only from sheep and from goats?
chunks.st: only from lambs and goats?

chunks.en: If so,

mishnayos.summary: There were seven measuring cups for liquids, from a hin down to a quarter log. Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok says one hin cup had lines marking the amounts. Rabbi Shimon says there was no hin cup, but a cup of a log and a half for the Kohen Gadol's mincha.

chunks.st: There were seven measuring vessels for liquids in the Temple.

chunks.en: a hin, and half a hin,

words.note: A measure of twelve log.

chunks.en: and a quarter log.

chunks.en: with which he measured for the mincha of the Kohen Gadol:

mishnayos.summary: The mishnah explains what the smaller cups were used for. The Sages say a mincha gets one log of oil for each issaron, but Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says every mincha gets just one log. It also lists the oil for the nesachim of a bull, ram and lamb, and for the Menorah.

chunks.en: What was the quarter log used for?
chunks.st: What purpose did the quarter-log measuring vessel serve?

chunks.en: A quarter log of water for a metzora,
chunks.st: It was used to measure a quarter-log of water for the purification of the leper,

chunks.en: and a quarter log of oil for a nazir.
chunks.st: and a quarter-log of oil for the wafers and loaves that the nazirite brings on the day that his term of naziriteship ends.

chunks.st: It was used to measure a half-log of water for the rite of the sota

chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov says:

chunks.st: requires only its single log of oil,

chunks.en: as it says (Vayikra 14):

chunks.st: “And a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering, and a log of oil” (Leviticus 14:21).
chunks.stMore: The juxtaposition of “a meal offering” with “a log of oil” teaches a principle for all meal offerings: Each offering requires only one log of oil. The mishna lists the quantities of oil and wine that were required for the meal offerings and libations that accompanied the sacrifice of an animal.

chunks.st: and four log, i.e., one-third of a hin, for those of a ram;

mishnayos.summary: Nesachim with the same amount of oil for the flour may be mixed together, but those of lambs may not be mixed with those of bulls and rams. If each was mixed with its own oil first, they are kosher. The lamb of the omer has a double mincha but regular nesachim.

chunks.en: We may mix the nesachim of rams with the nesachim of bulls,
chunks.st: One may mix together the libations of bulls with the libations of rams;
chunks.stMore: the meal offerings may be mixed as they both share the same ratio of flour to oil, i.e., two log of oil for each tenth of an ephah of flour.

chunks.en: the nesachim of lambs with the nesachim of lambs,
chunks.st: Likewise, one may mix together the libations of lambs with the libations of other lambs,
chunks.stMore: as the meal offerings both share the same ratio of three log of oil for each tenth of an ephah of flour.

chunks.en: those of a single person with those of the community,
chunks.st: And one may mix together the libations of the offering of an individual with those of a communal offering.

chunks.en: those of today with those of yesterday.
chunks.st: And one may mix together the libations of an offering brought on one day with those of the day before, if the meal offerings have the same ratio of oil to flour.

chunks.en: But we may not mix the nesachim
chunks.st: But one may not mix together the libations of

chunks.en: of lambs with the nesachim of bulls and rams.
chunks.st: lambs with the libations of bulls or the libations of rams, as the meal offerings have different ratios of oil to flour.

chunks.en: And if he mixed these by themselves
chunks.st: And nevertheless, if one intermingled the flour and oil of these lamb offerings by themselves

chunks.en: and those by themselves,
chunks.st: and the flour and oil of these bull or ram offerings by themselves,

chunks.en: and then they got mixed together, they are kosher.
chunks.st: and only then were they mixed together, then they remain fit to be sacrificed.

chunks.en: If it happened before he mixed them,
chunks.st: If they were mixed together before the oil and flour of each offering were independently intermingled to form the meal offering,

chunks.en: it is pasul. The lamb that comes with the omer,
chunks.st: then they are disqualified. With regard to the lamb offering that comes with the omer meal offering, which is accompanied by another meal offering and a wine libation,

chunks.en: even though its mincha is doubled,
chunks.st: even though the quantity of flour used in its meal offering is doubled,
chunks.stMore: i.e., one uses twice the amount that is generally used for meal offerings that accompany the sacrifice of a lamb,

chunks.en: its nesachim were not doubled.
chunks.st: its oil and wine libations were not doubled;
chunks.stMore: rather, three log of oil and three log of wine were used, per the standard quantities used for a lamb.

mishnayos.stIntro: Many animal offerings are brought together with a meal offering and a wine libation. These additions are collectively referred to as libations.

mishnayos.summary: The measuring cups were filled heaped up, except for the Kohen Gadol's. What spills over from liquid cups is holy, but not from dry cups. Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Yosei give different reasons.

chunks.en: All the measures that were in the Beis HaMikdash
chunks.st: All measuring vessels that were in the Temple were

chunks.en: were filled heaped up,
chunks.st: such that they held the volume that they measured when their contents were heaped above the rim,

chunks.en: except for that of the Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: except for the measuring vessel used to measure the flour for the griddle-cake offering of the High Priest,

chunks.en: whose heaped amount fit inside it.
chunks.st: as its heaped measure, i.e., the quantity of flour held by a tenth of an ephah measuring vessel when heaped, was contained within its walls when the flour was leveled with the rim.
chunks.stMore: This was due to the fact that the measuring vessel for the griddle-cake offering was slightly larger than the tenth of an ephah measuring vessel.

chunks.en: The measures for liquids:
chunks.st: With regard to measuring vessels for liquids,

chunks.en: what spills over them is holy.
chunks.st: their overflows, i.e., that which flows onto the outside of vessel’s walls, are sacred, but

chunks.en: And the measures for dry things:
chunks.st: with regard to measuring vessels for dry substances,

chunks.en: what spills over them is not holy.
chunks.st: their overflows are non-sacred.

words.note: Not holy.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says

chunks.en: The measures for liquids are holy,
chunks.st: that the reason for this difference is that since the measuring vessels for liquids are themselves sacred,

chunks.en: so what spills over them is holy.
chunks.st: therefore their overflows are sacred,

chunks.en: And the measures for dry things are not holy,
chunks.st: and since the measuring vessels for dry substances are non-sacred,

chunks.en: so what spills over them is not holy.
chunks.st: therefore their overflows are non-sacred.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: Not because of this,
chunks.st: The difference is not due to that factor.

chunks.en: but because the liquid moves around,
chunks.st: Rather, it is because the overflow of liquid was originally inside the vessel, where it became consecrated, and was then displaced,

chunks.en: and the dry does not move around.
chunks.st: whereas the overflow of a dry substance was not displaced from inside the vessel, so it had not become consecrated.

mishnayos.summary: All korbanos need nesachim, except the bechor, maaser, Pesach, chatas and asham. But the chatas and asham of a metzora do need nesachim.

chunks.he: כָּל קָרְבְּנוֹת הַצִּבּוּר וְהַיָּחִיד טְעוּנִין נְסָכִים,
chunks.en: All the korbanos of the community and of a single person need nesachim,
chunks.st: All offerings, whether communal or individual, require libations, i.e., a meal offering and a wine libation,

chunks.en: except for the bechor and the maaser,
chunks.st: except for the firstborn offering, the animal tithe offering,

words.note: A firstborn animal.
Every tenth animal of the flock.

chunks.en: and the Pesach, and the chatas, and the asham.
chunks.st: the Paschal offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering, with which libations are not brought.

words.note: A sin offering.

chunks.en: But the chatas of a metzora
chunks.st: But the exception to this exception is that the sin offering of a leper

chunks.en: and his asham need nesachim.
chunks.st: and his guilt offering do require libations.

mishnayos.summary: Korbanos of the community do not get semichah, except the bull for a mistake of the Beis Din and the goat sent away on Yom Kippur. Korbanos of one person do get semichah, except the bechor, maaser and Pesach. An heir can do semichah, bring nesachim, and make a temurah.

chunks.he: כָּל קָרְבְּנוֹת הַצִּבּוּר אֵין בָּהֶם סְמִיכָה,
chunks.en: All korbanos of the community have no semichah,
chunks.st: For all communal offerings there is no mitzva of placing hands on the head of the offering,

chunks.en: except for the bull that comes
chunks.st: except for the bull that comes

chunks.en: for all the mitzvos,
chunks.explain: When the Beis Din made a mistake and the people sinned.
chunks.st: to atone for a community-wide violation of any one of the mitzvot
chunks.stMore: that was perpetrated due to an erroneous ruling of the Sanhedrin, where the judges of the Sanhedrin are required to place their hands upon its head (see Leviticus 4:13–21);

chunks.en: and the goat sent away on Yom Kippur.
chunks.st: and the scapegoat

chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: All korbanos of a single person need semichah,
chunks.st: All offerings of an individual require placing hands,

chunks.en: except for the bechor, the maaser, and the Pesach.
chunks.st: except for the firstborn offering, the animal tithe offering, and the Paschal offering. The mitzva of placing hands is performed by the owner of the offering. The mishna adds:

chunks.en: And the heir does semichah, brings nesachim, and can make a temurah.
chunks.st: And if the owner died, then the heir is regarded as the offering’s owner and so he places his hands on the offering and brings the accompanying libations. And furthermore, he can substitute a non-sacred animal for it.
chunks.stMore: Although it is prohibited to perform an act of substitution, if the owner of an offering does this, his attempt is successful to the extent that the non-sacred animal is thereby consecrated, even though the original offering also remains sacred.

mishnayos.summary: Everyone who brings a korban does semichah, except some people who are not obligated. Semichah is an extra part of the mitzvah; it is done on the head with two hands, in the same place as the shechitah, right before it.

chunks.en: Everyone does semichah,
chunks.st: Everyone who brings an animal offering places hands upon its head,

chunks.en: except a deaf-mute,
chunks.st: except for a deaf-mute,

words.note: Someone who cannot hear or speak.

chunks.en: a shoteh, and a child,
chunks.st: an imbecile, a minor,

words.note: Someone whose mind does not work properly.

chunks.en: a blind person, and a non-Jew,
chunks.st: a blind person, a gentile,

chunks.en: and a slave, and a messenger,
chunks.st: a Canaanite slave, the agent of the owner of the offering who brings the offering on the owner’s behalf,

chunks.en: is an extra part of the mitzvah,

chunks.en: done on the head,

chunks.st: And immediately following the rite of placing hands, the slaughter is performed.

mishnayos.summary: Semichah and waving each have something stricter. One partner can wave for everyone, but each one must do his own semichah. Waving is done in more kinds of cases: for one person or the community, alive or after shechitah, and even for things that are not alive.

chunks.en: Semichah is stricter than waving in one way, and waving is stricter than semichah in another way.
chunks.st: There is an aspect of greater stringency with regard to placing hands than there is with regard to waving, and there is an aspect of greater stringency with regard to waving than there is with regard to placing hands.

chunks.en: For one person may wave for all the partners,
chunks.st: The stringency with regard to placing hands is that if several people are partners in bringing an offering, one of them waves the offering on behalf of all the other partners,

chunks.en: but one person may not do semichah for all the partners.
chunks.st: but one cannot fulfill the requirement of placing hands if he alone places hands on behalf of all the other partners; rather, each member must place hands himself.

chunks.en: And waving is stricter,
chunks.st: The stringency with regard to waving is

chunks.he: שֶׁהַתְּנוּפָה נוֹהֶגֶת בְּקָרְבְּנוֹת הַיָּחִיד וּבְקָרְבְּנוֹת הַצִּבּוּר,
chunks.en: because waving applies to korbanos of one person and to korbanos of the community,
chunks.st: that waving is practiced in the cases of both offerings of an individual, e.g., peace offerings, where the breast and thigh and sacrificial portions are waved, and in the cases of communal offerings, e.g., the two lambs sacrificed on Shavuot, which are waved together with the two loaves;

chunks.en: to ones that are alive and to ones that were shechted,
chunks.st: and it is practiced both in the cases of offerings when they are alive, e.g., the guilt offering of a leper and the lambs of Shavuot, and in the cases of offerings after they are slaughtered, e.g., the breast and thigh. By contrast, placing hands is practiced with a live animal.

chunks.en: to something that has a living spirit
chunks.st: A further stringency is that waving is practiced both in the case of an item in which there is a living spirit, i.e., an animal offering,

chunks.en: and to something that has no living spirit,
chunks.st: and in the case of an item in which there is not a living spirit,
chunks.stMore: e.g., the omer offering, the sota meal offering, and the loaves accompanying a thanks offering and the ram of the nazirite,

chunks.en: which is not so with semichah.
chunks.st: whereas placing hands is only ever performed upon living beings.

mishnayos.summary: The messengers of Beis Din prepared the barley for the omer before Yom Tov, and many people came to watch. After dark on the first night of Pesach, the reaper asked the crowd again and again if it was time and if he should cut. This was to show the Baysusim, who said the omer may not be cut right after Yom Tov, that they were wrong.

chunks.en: How would they do it?
chunks.st: How would they perform the rite of the harvest of the omer?

chunks.st: on the eve of the festival of Passover
